The migration reads it backwards — a stored Tailwind class becomes a name
(src-tauri/src/utils/quickcap_storage.rs). The card reads it forwards — a
stored name becomes classes to render (src/mini-apps/quickcap/parsing.ts).
Storing the name rather than the classes is the point of the change. A cap
written before 0.9.7 has a Tailwind class string frozen into the user's own
Markdown file, sometimes in frontmatter and sometimes as an HTML comment in
the body. That is a styling detail leaking into their data: restyle the app
and every cap's colour breaks, and anyone opening the vault in Obsidian sees
A value that is not in this table is left exactly as written rather than
guessed at — see the migration, which never invents a colour it cannot read.
